pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 03

Keys describe identity

A stable key helps React match an item to its previous instance within a list of siblings. Reordering should not make one item inherit the local state of another.

items.map(item => (
<Row key={item.id} item={item} />
));

An array index can be a poor key when items move, are inserted or removed. A freshly generated random key also destroys continuity between renders.

Practice: explain why editing a row can reveal a bad key choice.

System Design

Start with the job

Before drawing components, establish who uses the system, what they need to do, and what failure would mean. An architecture solves a particular set of constraints.

Need Constraint Decision

For a personal PDF reader, local access, data integrity and fast navigation may matter more than multi-region availability. Do not pay for complexity that the task does not require.

A useful question: what must still work when the internet does not?

Caching is a tradeoff

A cache avoids repeating work, but introduces a second representation that can become stale. Decide what is authoritative, how entries are invalidated and how much memory the cache may use.

PDF thumbnails are derived data. If a thumbnail disappears, recreate it. Original documents and private annotations are not disposable caches.

Original Thumbnail Display

Ask: can this information be recreated without asking the user to do the work again?

SHELF SAMPLES / 04

Design the failure path

An import is not complete when a preview appears. It is complete when the required data has been safely stored and the operation has been acknowledged.

A recoverable design considers full storage, interrupted writes, duplicate requests and corrupted input. Error messages must tell the user what happened without claiming that missing work was saved.

This is original sample material illustrating general engineering reasoning. The architecture and recovery semantics of this app are documented in the source package.

Review exercise: sketch a save operation that can fail at any step without overwriting the original.

pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 01

JavaScript Deep Dive

Know the return shape

Choosing an array method starts with the shape you need back. One item, a new array and a yes-or-no answer are different results.

items.find(test);   // item or undefined
items.filter(test); // array
items.some(test);   // boolean
items.every(test);  // boolean

Find selects the first matching value. Filter creates an array containing matching values. Some asks whether a match exists; every asks whether all visited items pass.

A boolean cannot be followed by .map(). Check the return value before chaining methods.

SHELF  /  ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 1

SHELF SAMPLES / 02

Return is not decoration
With an arrow function, an expression body returns its
expression. A block body needs an explicit return
statement.
const a = [1, 2].map(n => n * 2);
// [2, 4]
const b = [1, 2].map(n => { n * 2; });
// [undefined, undefined]

The multiplication in the second example happens,
but its value is not returned by the callback. Map
collects the callback results.
Close the document and explain this bug out loud
before checking the code again.

SHELF / ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES

pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 04

Change a value, keep the original

To update an item without mutating the source array, create a new array and a new object for the item that changes.

const updated = games.map(game =>
game.title === "Eclipse"
? { ...game, favorite: true }
: game
);

Unchanged objects are reused here. This is a shallow update, not a deep clone of every nested object.

Primary reading: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Referen ce/Global_Objects/Array developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Closures

SHELF SAMPLES / 02

Trace the program
Read a short program in execution order. Track the
value produced by each expression and the value
returned by each function.
const numbers = [1, 2, 3];
const kept = numbers.filter(n => n > 1);
const doubled = kept.map(n => n * 2);
console.log(doubled); // [4, 6]

A useful trace records both type and value. A result
can look semantically related to the task while having
the wrong shape for the next operation.
Try the same reasoning with no matching numbers.
Does your chain still work?

pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 03

Test the boundary

Test cases should probe the assumptions, not merely confirm the example used while writing the code. Include the smallest input, a repeated value and a case that challenges ordering.

function firstEven(values) {
return values.find(value => value % 2 === 0);
}
firstEven([]);       // undefined
firstEven([3, 5]);   // undefined
firstEven([3, 4, 2]); // 4

Explain what the caller should do when a result is undefined.

SHELF  /  ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 3

SHELF SAMPLES / 04

Explain the tradeoff

A technically correct solution is only part of the conversation. Explain the assumptions, the chosen approach and the cost as the input grows.

Avoid claiming that one implementation is faster without defining the input, runtime and measurement. Simpler code can be the better default until a demonstrated bottleneck requires more work.

These are original sample practice notes. No scoring, generated questions or interview simulation is running inside Shelf.

Write one note: what would make you change your chosen solution?

Computer Science Essentials

A model is a simplification

A useful model keeps the details that affect a decision and leaves out those that do not. It should help you reason, not merely give something a more impressive name.

For example, describing a stack as last-in, first-out helps predict which item is removed next. The description is useful before deciding how to store the stack.

Push A Push B Pop B

Use a tiny concrete example before introducing an abstraction.

pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 02

Growth, not a stopwatch

Time complexity describes how work grows with input size under a stated model. It does not predict the exact time on a particular device.

A linear scan may inspect every element. A binary search repeatedly narrows a sorted search space. The latter relies on a precondition: the data must have a compatible ordering.

Ask whether preparation and sorting costs are included in the analysis.

SHELF  /  ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 2

SHELF SAMPLES / 03

References and copies
Two variables can refer to the same mutable object.
Changing that object through one variable is visible
through the other reference.
const a = { score: 1 };
const b = a;
b.score = 2;
console.log(a.score); // 2

Copying an outer object with spread does not
automatically copy its nested objects. The boundary
between shared and copied data matters.
Draw two arrows pointing to the same object. The bug
becomes easier to see.

SHELF SAMPLES / 04

Use the right structure

The important question is not which data structure is most sophisticated. It is which operations must be cheap, which ordering matters and what guarantees the caller needs.

A library may keep its original files by stable identifier while maintaining a separate searchable metadata representation. Different representations serve different operations.

Original sample material. JavaScript reference semantics: developer.mozilla. org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Working_with_objects

Before optimizing, list the three operations your application performs most often.

One reason to change

Keep rendering, workflow decisions and durable storage separate. A typography change should not require editing a file-import transaction.

Small files help, but file length alone does not guarantee good boundaries. A module should expose a coherent contract and avoid leaking details that callers do not need.

Try naming a module without using the words manager, helper or utils.

pages.text:
SHELF SAMPLES / 03

Depend on a contract

An application workflow can depend on a storage contract instead of constructing a specific database or file store. The composition root supplies the concrete implementation.

protocol LibraryPersistence {
func load() throws -> Library
func save(_ library: Library) throws
}

This keeps tests focused. A storage failure can be introduced deliberately without filling the device or corrupting real user files.

Test that an unsuccessful save does not leak uncommitted in-memory state.

SHELF  /  ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 3

Use patterns sparingly

Every abstraction introduces a concept that the next engineer must learn. Add the boundary when it protects a responsibility, enables an important test or isolates a volatile dependency.

Keep the simplest implementation that meets the real constraints. An offline personal library does not need a distributed backend to look or feel well made.

pages.text:
The mid-level answer engine

1. WHAT?

Give a clean definition with the correct noun. “A CDN is a geographically distributed delivery/cache layer...”

2. WHY?

Name the engineering pressure it solves: latency, correctness, maintainability, concurrency, cost, security...

3. EXAMPLE?

Make it concrete in ordinary product code. Browser → API → cache → database beats abstract vocabulary.

4. TRADE-OFF?

Say what it costs or when you would not use it. Mid-level engineers know tools create new problems too.

5. FAILURE MODE?

Show that you can operate software, not just design happy paths: stale cache, race, retry storm, leaked secret, slow query...

How apps wait, stream, schedule, and react without freezing.

The language behaviors behind most interview gotchas.

06 TYPESCRIPT & REACT FOUNDATIONS

Types, components, state, effects, identity, and reuse.

07 FRONTEND PLATFORM, UX & PERFORMANCE

Rendering, accessibility, loading, navigation, and perceived

speed.

HTTP is a stateless request-response protocol. I use methods, headers, status codes, and bodies to define the contract between client and server.

HTTPS

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

HTTP carried through TLS so traffic is encrypted and the server can prove its identity. It protects credentials, tokens, and user data from easy interception or tampering.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

HTTP is shouting your password across a cafe. HTTPS is whispering through a locked tube.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

https://example.com/login encrypts the request
while it travels over the network.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. TLS gives confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Port

A numeric identifier that distinguishes services on the same host. One machine can run a web app, database, cache, and more at the same IP.

A port selects the service or process at a host address; the combination of protocol, host, and port helps identify an endpoint.

An HTTP request contains a method, target URL, headers, and optionally a body.

009 WEB, NETWORKING & DELIVERY

HTTP methods

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Standard verbs that express what operation a request intends to perform. They make API contracts predictable and communicate semantics to clients, caches, and infrastructure.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

GET looks, POST creates, PATCH edits, DELETE throws it in the bin.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

GET /users reads; POST /users creates; PATCH /
users/42 updates part; DELETE removes.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I use HTTP methods according to their semantics: GET for retrieval, POST for creation/actions, PUT for replacement, PATCH for partial updates, DELETE for removal.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

010 WEB, NETWORKING & DELIVERY

HTTP status codes

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Three-digit codes that summarize the outcome of an HTTP response. They let clients handle success, redirects, client errors, and server errors consistently.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A restaurant scorecard: 2xx "here is dinner", 4xx "you ordered nonsense", 5xx "the kitchen is on fire".

R E A L   E X A M P L E

200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad
Request, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, 503.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I treat 2xx as success, 4xx as client-side request/auth issues, and 5xx as server-side failures; specific codes matter for client behavior.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Headers

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Metadata fields attached to HTTP requests and responses. They carry information such as content type, authorization, caching rules, and tracing IDs.

The parcel label is not the gift; it says what is inside and where it should go.

Authorization: Bearer ..., Content-Type:
application/json, Cache-Control: max-age=3600.

Headers carry protocol metadata separate from the main payload, for example auth, caching, content negotiation, and correlation IDs.

The request body contains payload data, typically JSON or form data, for operations that create or modify resources.

GET /products?

I use query parameters for optional modifiers such as filters, sort order, search terms, and pagination.

Path parameters usually identify a concrete resource, while query parameters usually modify how a collection is retrieved.

CORS is a browser security mechanism based on server response headers. It is not authentication and it does not stop non-browser clients.

A reverse proxy is the public entry point in front of servers. I use it for routing, TLS termination, load balancing, caching, and security controls.

TTL

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Time To Live: how long a cached or leased value remains valid before expiring. It bounds staleness and prevents data from living forever.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A carton says "good for 60 seconds"; after that, throw it away and get a fresh one.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

TTL is an expiration policy. Short TTLs improve freshness; long TTLs improve hit rate but increase staleness risk.

038 SECURITY, IDENTITY & TRUST

HttpOnly cookie

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A cookie marked so browser JavaScript cannot read it. It reduces exposure of session secrets to JavaScript during many XSS scenarios.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The cookie is in a locked lunchbox: the browser can deliver it, but your JS cannot open it.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Set-Cookie: session=abc; HttpOnly; Secure.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

HttpOnly prevents client-side JavaScript from reading a cookie, which is useful for session credentials, though it does not eliminate XSS impact.

039 SECURITY, IDENTITY & TRUST

JWT

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A compact signed token format containing claims, represented as header.payload.signature. It lets a recipient verify that claims were issued by a trusted signer without a database lookup for every verification.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A concert wristband says "VIP" and has an unforgeable stamp; anyone can read VIP, but they cannot fake the stamp.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Authorization: Bearer <jwt> containing sub, exp,
and roles.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

JWTs are signed claim containers, not automatically encrypted. I validate signature, issuer, audience, and expiry rather than trusting decoded payloads.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

041 SECURITY, IDENTITY & TRUST

Refresh token

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A longer-lived credential used to obtain new access tokens without asking the user to sign in again. It balances user convenience with short-lived access credentials.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Your train season pass lets you print today's ticket; you do not wave the season pass at every ticket gate.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

When access token expires, client sends refresh
token to auth server for a new access token.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A refresh token is higher-value and longer-lived than an access token, so I protect it carefully, rotate it where appropriate, and restrict its use to the token endpoint.

A one-way transformation that maps input to a fixed-length digest; password hashing uses deliberately slow, salted algorithms. Passwords should be verified without storing recoverable plaintext.

the submitted password.

Hashing is one-way. For passwords I use a password-hashing function such as Argon2 or bcrypt with a salt, not fast general-purpose hashes.

044 SECURITY, IDENTITY & TRUST

XSS

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Cross-Site Scripting: untrusted content causes attacker-controlled script or dangerous markup to execute in a user's browser context. It can steal data, perform actions as the user, or alter the UI.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Someone sneaks a tiny evil robot into a note that your website blindly turns on.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Avoid raw innerHTML with user input; React
escapes text by default; sanitize trusted HTML
when raw HTML is necessary.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

XSS is code injection into the browser. I prevent it with contextual escaping, safe DOM APIs/framework defaults, CSP as defense-in-depth, and careful HTML sanitization.

048 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY

Database

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A system for persistently storing, querying, and updating application data. Applications need durable state that survives process restarts.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Your app's memory is a goldfish; the database is the notebook it writes everything into.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

An operation that combines rows from related tables based on a condition. Normalized relational data is intentionally split across tables and must often be recombined when queried.

ON u.id=o.user_id.

JOINs combine related rows. I know INNER JOIN for matching rows and LEFT JOIN when I need all left-side rows even without matches.

054 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY

Transaction

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A group of database operations treated as a single logical unit that commits or rolls back. It prevents partial updates that would leave business data inconsistent.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Moving a cake: either the whole cake reaches the table or we pretend the move never happened; half a cake is not a valid transaction.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Debit account A and credit account B inside
BEGIN...COMMIT; on failure ROLLBACK.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Transactions make related writes atomic and provide isolation guarantees so partial business operations are not persisted.

ACID

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A mnemonic for transaction properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. It summarizes the guarantees expected from robust transactional databases.

A = all-or-nothing; C = rules stay sane; I = shoppers do not trample each other; D = the receipt survives a power cut.

A committed order survives restart; concurrent
updates respect the chosen isolation level.

ACID describes transactional guarantees. I pay particular attention to isolation level and business invariants rather than treating the acronym as magic.

056 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY

Race condition

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A bug where correctness depends on the unpredictable timing/interleaving of concurrent operations. Concurrent requests can both make decisions from stale state.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two people see the last donut, both shout "mine", and both somehow leave with a donut receipt.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Stock=1; requests A and B both read 1 before
either decrements. Use transaction/locking/
atomic update.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A race condition occurs when concurrent operations access shared state without sufficient coordination. I fix the invariant, not just add random delays.

057 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY

Optimistic locking

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A concurrency strategy that allows reads freely but rejects an update if the record changed since it was read. It avoids heavy locks when conflicts are uncommon.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You edit a shared document version 7; if someone already saved version 8, your version 7 save is rejected.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

UPDATE docs SET ..., version=8 WHERE id=1 AND
version=7; zero rows means conflict.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Optimistic locking detects conflicts using a version/ timestamp and asks the caller to retry or resolve when concurrent changes occur.

060 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY

Cursor pagination

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Pagination that continues after a stable sort key or opaque cursor rather than a row count. It handles large, changing feeds more efficiently and consistently.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Bookmark the last book you read instead of counting 4,820 books from the entrance every time.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

GET /feed?after=opaqueCursor; query uses WHERE
created_at < lastSeen ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Cursor/keyset pagination uses the last sort position, avoiding large offsets and reducing duplicate/missing items in changing datasets. SECTION

JavaScript event loop

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The runtime mechanism that coordinates the call stack with queued asynchronous callbacks/jobs. It explains ordering, responsiveness, and why long synchronous tasks freeze JavaScript UIs.

One chef cooks one active dish at a time; assistants handle timers and deliveries, then put finished tickets back in the chef's queue.

Promise callbacks enter the microtask queue;
timers run from a task queue after the stack is
clear.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

JavaScript runs synchronous code on a call stack. The event loop schedules queued work when the stack is free, with microtasks processed at defined checkpoints.

069 REALTIME & ASYNC JAVASCRIPT

Microtask queue

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The high-priority job queue used for Promise reactions and related microtasks. It affects exact async ordering and can starve later tasks if abused.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

VIP queue: promise callbacks enter before the next normal timer gets its turn.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

console.log("A");
Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log("B"));
console.log("C") => A,C,B.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Promise callbacks run as microtasks. After the current stack finishes, the runtime drains microtasks before moving to the next task such as a timer.

071 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS

async / await

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Syntax for writing Promise-based asynchronous code in a sequential-looking style. It makes async control flow and error handling easier to read.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You write "wait for pizza" in the recipe, but the whole restaurant does not freeze while your pizza bakes.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const r = await fetch(url); const data = await
r.json();

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

async/await is syntax over Promises. await suspends the async function until settlement; it does not block the JavaScript runtime from processing other work.

072 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS

try / catch

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Language syntax for handling exceptions thrown during execution, including rejected promises when awaited. It lets code recover, translate, log, or surface errors deliberately.

Put a trampoline under the risky acrobat so a fall becomes a handled event instead of chaos.

try { await save(); } catch (err)
{ showError(err); }

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

try/catch handles exceptions. With async/await it catches rejected awaited Promises, and I avoid swallowing errors without context.

075 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS

var, let, const

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

JavaScript declaration forms with different scoping and reassignment behavior. Choosing predictable declarations reduces bugs and communicates intent.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

const is "do not replace this box"; let is "this label

may point somewhere else"; var is the weird uncle from older JavaScript.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const user = {...}; let page = 1; avoid var in
modern application code.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I default to const, use let when reassignment is required, and avoid var because of function scope and hoisting behavior.

Hoisting

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

JavaScript's declaration processing behavior that makes some bindings/functions known before the line where they are declared. It explains surprising access rules and the temporal dead zone.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The theater has your name on the seating chart before you sit down, but security may still stop you entering early.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Function declarations can be called before their
textual declaration; let/const cannot be
accessed before initialization.

Declarations are processed before execution, but behavior differs: function declarations are callable early, while let/const are in the temporal dead zone until initialized.

077 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS

Primitive values

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

JavaScript values that are not objects: string, number, boolean, undefined, null, bigint, and symbol. Their copy/equality behavior differs from objects.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A primitive is like a printed number on a card; copying the card gives you another value, not a shared mutable box.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

let a=5; let b=a; b=9 does not change a.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Primitives are immutable value types. Assigning them copies the value, unlike object references that can point to shared mutable objects.

Reference semantics

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Objects are accessed through references, so multiple variables can refer to the same underlying object. It explains mutation bugs and React identity behavior.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two remote controls point at the same TV; pressing either changes the same screen.

const a={x:1}; const b=a; b.x=2; now a.x is 2.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Object variables hold references. Copying the reference does not clone the object, so mutation is visible through every reference to it.

Mutation

Changing an existing object, array, or other mutable structure in place. Mutation can be efficient but makes shared-state reasoning harder.

Mutation changes existing state in place. In React state I avoid direct mutation because identity changes are important for predictable updates.

091 TYPESCRIPT & REACT FOUNDATIONS

TypeScript

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

JavaScript plus a static type system checked before runtime. It catches many integration mistakes earlier and documents contracts for humans and tools.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

JavaScript lets you put soup in a USB port; TypeScript yells before you try.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

function add(a:number,b:number):number { return
a+b; }

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

TypeScript adds static checking and developer tooling but erases to JavaScript at runtime; it cannot replace runtime validation of untrusted data.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Interface

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A TypeScript declaration describing the expected shape/capabilities of an object or class. It makes contracts explicit and reusable.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

R E A L   E X A M P L E

interface User { id:number; name:string }

An interface describes a structural contract. TypeScript is structurally typed, so compatible shapes can satisfy the interface.

Union types model alternatives. Combined with discriminated unions, they make impossible states harder to represent.

React component

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A reusable unit that describes UI from props, state, and context. Components let interfaces be composed from focused pieces.

A Lego instruction booklet for one UI piece: give it data, it tells React what that piece should look like.

<article>{user.name}</article>; }

A React component is a function that returns a description of UI. I keep rendering pure and move side effects to appropriate boundaries.

useEffect

A React hook for synchronizing a component with systems outside React after rendering. It is the correct boundary for subscriptions, imperative APIs, timers, and similar external synchronization.

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The function returned from an effect to undo the previous subscription/resource before rerun or unmount. It prevents duplicate listeners, stale subscriptions, and leaks.

Prop drilling is not automatically bad. I tolerate simple explicit passing and introduce context/composition/store only when the dependency is genuinely cross-cutting.

Debouncing

Delaying an action until a burst of events has been quiet for a chosen interval. It avoids firing expensive work for every keystroke.

Debounce waits for inactivity before running. It is good for search/autosave, but I still handle stale requests and cancellation.

Lazy loading

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Deferring loading or initialization until a resource is actually needed. It reduces initial work and improves startup performance.

Lazy loading moves non-critical work off the initial path. I balance smaller startup cost against later loading states and network waterfalls.

Retry

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Attempting a failed operation again when the failure may be temporary. Transient network/service errors often succeed later.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

If the vending machine says "network hiccup", try once more; if it says "invalid coin", repeating 40 times is not intelligence.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Retry 503/timeouts; do not blindly retry a 400
validation error.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I retry only transient failures, cap attempts, make operations idempotent where necessary, and combine retries with backoff/jitter.

Exponential backoff

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A retry strategy where delays grow after consecutive failures, often with random jitter. It gives a recovering service breathing room and avoids synchronized retry storms.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Knock again after 1s, then 2s, then 4s - do not machine-gun the doorbell.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Retry delays 500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s plus random
jitter.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Exponential backoff reduces pressure during outages; jitter prevents many clients from retrying in lockstep.

143 RELIABILITY, ARCHITECTURE & DELIVERY

Idempotency

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once. Networks retry, users double-click, and clients time out after servers already committed work.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Pressing the elevator button 12 times should not summon 12 elevators.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Payment request includes Idempotency-Key so a

Providing dependencies from outside a module/class instead of constructing concrete dependencies internally. It improves testability and allows implementations to be swapped.

Dependency injection inverts construction responsibility. It makes dependencies explicit and lets tests substitute fakes without patching globals.

Big O describes growth rate, not exact runtime. I use it to reason about scalability while still profiling real code.

173 COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING JUDGMENT

Object vs Map

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Objects are general JavaScript records; Map is a dedicated key-value collection with arbitrary key types and explicit iteration APIs. The choice affects key semantics, iteration, and intent.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Object is a labeled cupboard built into the house; Map is a purpose-built key locker.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const cache=new Map();
cache.set(userObject,result);
cache.get(userObject).

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I use plain objects for record-like JSON-shaped data and Map when I need dynamic keyed collections, non-string keys, predictable iteration, or Map APIs.

186 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Type inference

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

TypeScript can often determine a value's type without you writing it explicitly. It reduces noise while preserving static checking.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

If the waiter already sees you holding a coffee, you do not need to label it “coffee” three times.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Type inference lets TypeScript derive types from values and usage. I annotate public boundaries and complex cases, but avoid redundant annotations.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Do not annotate everything just to “look typed”; let inference work.

187 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

any

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type that effectively disables TypeScript checking for that value. It is an escape hatch for migrations or truly untyped boundaries, but it spreads risk.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

any is giving a raccoon a master key and saying “probably fine.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

let payload: any; payload.flyToMoon(); //
compiler shrugs

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

any opts out of type safety. I keep it contained at boundaries and prefer unknown when I must accept untrusted values.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

If any flows through your app, TypeScript cannot protect downstream code.

unknown

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A safe top type: a value may be anything, but you must narrow it before using it. It models untrusted inputs without abandoning type safety.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A mystery box may contain a sandwich or a cobra; inspect it before biting.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

function parse(x: unknown) { if (typeof x ===
"string") return x.trim(); }

unknown is safer than any because consumers must prove what the value is before using it.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Great for JSON, errors, postMessage, and external data boundaries.

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type representing values that should never occur. It models impossible states and enables exhaustive checks.

The “dragon enters payroll form” branch should be impossible; never lets the compiler complain if it becomes possible.

never represents an impossible value. I often use it in exhaustive discriminated-union switches.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Type narrowing

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The process of refining a broad type into a more specific one using runtime checks. It lets TypeScript safely understand what operations are valid.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Security checks the costume at the door before deciding whether you are the chef or the magician.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

value.toUpperCase();

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Narrowing uses control flow, typeof, in, instanceof, or custom guards to move from broad types to precise ones.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Narrow at boundaries rather than scattering unsafe casts.

Type guard

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A runtime check that also teaches TypeScript a more specific type. It centralizes validation and improves downstream ergonomics.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A bouncer checks the wristband and announces “yes, this is definitely VIP.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

function isUser(x: unknown): x is User
{ return !!x && typeof x === "object" && "id" in
x; }

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A type guard combines runtime validation with a type predicate so the compiler can narrow values safely.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A guard is only trustworthy if the runtime check is actually strong enough.

192 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Discriminated union

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A union whose members share a literal tag such as status or type. It makes state machines and UI states explicit and exhaustively checkable.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Every suitcase has a giant sticker: LOADING, SUCCESS, or ERROR. No guessing what is inside.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

type State = {status:"loading"}|
{status:"success";data:User[]}|
{status:"error";error:Error};

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Discriminated unions model mutually exclusive states and let TypeScript narrow from a stable tag.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Excellent alternative to several booleans that can form impossible combinations.

193 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Structural typing

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Type compatibility is based mainly on shape rather than explicit inheritance names. It makes TypeScript flexible with plain JavaScript objects.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

If it has the right plug, voltage, and pins, TypeScript cares less about the brand printed on the charger.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

type Named={name:string}; const
x={name:"Ada",age:36}; const n:Named=x;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

TypeScript is structurally typed: values are compatible when their required shapes are compatible.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Useful flexibility, but accidental compatibility can happen with very similar shapes.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 193 / 310

keyof

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type operator that produces a union of the property names of another type. It lets APIs accept only valid keys.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Instead of letting someone request any drawer in the universe, hand them the exact list of drawers in this cabinet.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

| ...

keyof turns object keys into a type-level union, which is useful for safe property utilities and generic APIs.

195 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

typeof in type space

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

TypeScript can derive a type from an existing JavaScript value. It keeps runtime constants and compile-time types synchronized.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Write the restaurant menu once; the waiter and kitchen both read the same menu.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const config={mode:"prod",retries:3}; type
Config=typeof config;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

typeof in a type position derives a static type from a value, avoiding duplicated declarations.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Remember runtime typeof and type-space typeof are related but used in different contexts.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 195 / 310

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

197 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Mapped type

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type that transforms every property of another type. It powers reusable transformations such as optional, readonly, or boolean flag maps.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A tiny robot walks every apartment door and replaces each nameplate using the same rule.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

type Flags<T> = { [K in keyof T]: boolean };

Mapped types iterate over keys at the type level to build related object shapes.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Utility types like Partial and Readonly are based on this idea.

198 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Conditional type

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type-level if/else based on assignability. It enables expressive generic transformations.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The type checker asks: “is this animal a duck? If yes, give it pond rules; otherwise land rules.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

type IdOf<T> = T extends {id: infer I} ? I :
never;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Conditional types select different result types based on input types and are powerful in generic libraries.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Use sparingly; clever conditional types can become harder to maintain than the code they protect.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 198 / 310

199 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Utility types

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Built-in helpers such as Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, Required, and Readonly. They derive related types without duplicating interfaces.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Instead of photocopying a form and crossing out 18 fields, ask the copier for “only name and email.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Utility types transform existing types and keep related contracts synchronized.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Prefer deriving from a source type when the relationship is real; do not create accidental coupling.

Generic constraint

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A rule that limits what types a generic parameter may accept. It preserves reuse while guaranteeing required capabilities.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Anyone can join the dance class, but everyone must at least have a pulse.

{ return x.id; }

Generic constraints let reusable code demand the minimum shape it needs while preserving the caller's more specific type.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Constrain to capabilities, not unnecessarily concrete types.

satisfies operator

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Checks that a value conforms to a type while preserving the value's narrower inferred type. It validates config objects without throwing away useful literal information.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A suitcase passes airline size rules without replacing the exact contents list with “generic luggage.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const routes = {home:"/"} satisfies
Record<string,string>;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

satisfies validates assignability while keeping precise inference, which is ideal for configuration objects.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Different from “as”: satisfies checks; a cast can simply assert.

202 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Type assertion

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A developer instruction telling TypeScript to treat a value as a particular type. Sometimes necessary at trusted boundaries, but it does not perform runtime validation.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Writing “definitely a tiger” on a cardboard box does not make the animal inside a tiger.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const el = document.querySelector("#app") as
HTMLDivElement;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A type assertion changes the compiler's view, not the runtime value. I use it only when I have stronger knowledge than the compiler.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Avoid using assertions to silence real uncertainty.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 202 / 310

203 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Readonly

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A type-level restriction preventing mutation through a particular reference. It communicates intent and reduces accidental state changes.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The museum gives you gloves and says: admire the dinosaur, do not rearrange its bones.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

function render(user: Readonly<User>) { /*
cannot assign user.name */ }

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Readonly expresses non-mutating contracts. It helps document data flow but is not deep runtime immutability by itself.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Readonly is compile-time protection, not Object.freeze.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 203 / 310

Declaration file (.d.ts)

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A file containing TypeScript type declarations without runtime implementation. It describes JavaScript libraries, globals, and module APIs to the compiler.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The .d.ts is the instruction manual; the JavaScript package is the actual washing machine.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

declare module "legacy-lib" { export function
parse(x:string): Result }

Declaration files describe runtime APIs to TypeScript and are how many JavaScript libraries become type-safe to consume.

Types can be correct syntactically yet still lie about runtime behavior.

205 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES

Runtime validation vs static types

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

TypeScript checks code before execution; runtime validation checks real incoming values while the program runs. External data can violate your TypeScript declarations.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A blueprint says the bridge holds 10 tons; runtime validation is weighing the truck before it drives on.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const json: unknown = await res.json();
validateUser(json);

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

TypeScript does not validate network data at runtime. I validate untrusted boundaries and then narrow into trusted domain types.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

This distinction is a frequent source of production bugs.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 205 / 310

206 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

State colocation

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Keep state as close as possible to the components that actually need it. It reduces unnecessary coupling and rerenders.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Do not store your toothbrush in city hall because three roommates might someday need it.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

A modal's open state lives beside the modal
trigger, not in a global store.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I colocate state by default and lift or globalize it only when multiple distant consumers truly share ownership.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Global state is convenient until every feature can mutate everything.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 206 / 310

207 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Lifting state up

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Move shared state to the nearest common owner of components that need it. It creates one source of truth for coordinated UI.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two kids fighting over the thermostat need one thermostat, not two fake thermostats.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Parent owns selectedId; sibling list sets it and
detail pane reads it.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I lift state to the lowest common ancestor when siblings need coordinated access.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Do not lift farther than necessary.

208 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Client state vs server state

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Client state is local UI/application state; server state is remote data owned by the backend. They have different lifecycles, freshness, caching, and synchronization needs.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Your sticky-note “sidebar open” is yours; the bank balance belongs to the bank.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

useState for dialogOpen; query cache for GET /
users.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I separate client state from server state because remote data needs fetching, caching, invalidation, retries, and freshness semantics.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Treating API data like ordinary local state creates duplicated synchronization logic.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 208 / 310

Reducer

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A pure function that computes next state from current state and an action. It centralizes transition rules.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The vending machine receives “COIN” and current state, then deterministically decides the next state.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

function reducer(state,action)
{ switch(action.type){...} }

A reducer makes state transitions explicit and testable: nextState = reducer(state, action).

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Keep reducers pure; side effects belong outside.

211 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Stale closure

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A callback captures values from an older render and later uses outdated data. It explains many timer, effect, and async React bugs.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You text a friend directions from last Tuesday while the restaurant moved yesterday.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

setInterval(() => console.log(count),1000)
inside an effect with the wrong dependencies.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A stale closure happens when a callback closes over an older render's values. I fix the ownership/dependency model rather than blindly suppressing lint rules.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Functional state updates and refs solve some cases, but not every stale-closure problem.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 211 / 310

212 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

AbortController

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A browser API used to cancel fetches and other abortable operations. It prevents unnecessary work and stale responses from winning races.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You cancel the pizza order after realizing you ordered it to your old apartment.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const c=new AbortController(); fetch(url,
{signal:c.signal}); return ()=>c.abort();

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I abort obsolete requests during cleanup when user navigation or rapidly changing inputs can make previous work irrelevant.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Cancellation is different from merely ignoring a late result.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 212 / 310

213 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Async request race

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Two requests overlap and an older response arrives after a newer one, overwriting fresh UI. Fast typing, route changes, and filters can create incorrect data even when every request succeeds.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You ask “weather Berlin?” then “weather Rome?”; Berlin answers last and your Rome screen shows Berlin rain.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

query A starts, query B starts, B returns, A
returns -> stale overwrite.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I guard async races by cancellation, request identity, or a server-state library that tracks query keys and staleness.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

“Last response wins” is not always “latest intent wins.”

Explain it aloud before swiping. 213 / 310

214 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Component composition

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Build larger UI by combining focused components instead of adding endless configuration flags to one component. It keeps APIs flexible and reduces giant conditional components.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

LEGO bricks compose better than one 900-button “universal brick.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

<Dialog><Dialog.Title/><Dialog.Body/></Dialog>

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I prefer composition when consumers need flexible structure; it often scales better than a component with dozens of boolean props.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Too many tiny wrappers can also obscure the UI; use meaningful boundaries.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 214 / 310

Headless component

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Headless components are useful when teams need robust behavior and accessibility with custom presentation.

217 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Portal

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Render a React subtree into a different DOM container while keeping it in the same React tree. Useful for overlays that must escape clipping or stacking contexts.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The actor belongs to Scene A but enters through a trapdoor on a different part of the physical stage.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

createPortal(<Dialog/>, document.body)

Portals solve DOM placement issues for modals and tooltips while preserving React context and event semantics.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Portals do not magically solve accessibility, focus management, or z-index architecture.

Suspense

Suspense defines a loading boundary for compatible asynchronous resources or lazy components.

219 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Transition

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A lower-priority React update that can be interrupted so urgent interactions stay responsive. It helps expensive non-urgent UI updates avoid blocking typing/ click feedback.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The cashier serves the person at the desk before reorganizing the entire cereal aisle.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

startTransition(()=>setFilter(next));

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Transitions mark updates as non-urgent so React can prioritize immediate interactions and keep the interface responsive.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A transition does not make expensive computation free; profile real bottlenecks.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 219 / 310

220 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

useDeferredValue

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Lets a derived part of UI lag behind an urgent value temporarily. It keeps input responsive when downstream rendering is expensive.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Your mouth says the new word instantly; the giant scoreboard updates a moment later.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query);

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

useDeferredValue lets non-urgent rendering trail an urgent value, which can improve responsiveness for expensive result views.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Debouncing changes when work begins; deferring changes rendering priority - not the same thing.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 220 / 310

221 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Memoization boundary

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A deliberate place where stable inputs can allow expensive work or child rendering to be reused. It can reduce repeated computation, but adds complexity and comparison overhead.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You laminate a frequently used map instead of redrawing Europe every time someone asks where France is.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

React.memo(Chart), useMemo(expensiveProjection)

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I memoize after identifying a meaningful cost and stable inputs, rather than wrapping every function and component by habit.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Incorrect dependencies can create stale results; unnecessary memoization can make code worse.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 221 / 310

Referential stability

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Whether the same object/function reference is preserved across renders. React memoization and effect dependencies often use reference identity.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two identical-looking hotel keys are still different physical keys.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Referential stability matters when consumers compare by identity, such as memoized children or effect dependencies.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Do not stabilize references unless identity actually matters.

State machine

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

An explicit model of allowed states and transitions. It prevents impossible UI combinations in complex flows.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

An elevator can be MOVING or DOOR_OPEN, but it should not be both.

For complex flows I model explicit states and transitions instead of independent booleans whose combinations can become invalid.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A full state-machine library is optional; the mental model itself is valuable.

224 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Render purity

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A React render should calculate UI from inputs without causing external side effects. Pure rendering lets React safely rerun, pause, or discard work.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A restaurant menu printer may print the menu twice; it must not charge your card each time it prints.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Do not call fetch-and-write or localStorage
mutation directly during render.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

React rendering should be pure: same props/state/ context should describe the same UI without external mutations.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Development behaviors may intentionally render more than once to expose impurity.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 224 / 310

226 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Error recovery boundary

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A UI boundary designed not just to show an error but to offer a meaningful recovery path. Production UX should degrade locally rather than turning the whole page into a dead end.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

If the toaster breaks, you replace breakfast - you do not evacuate the entire house.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Widget error -> retry button; editor error ->
preserve draft and reload component.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I place error boundaries around meaningful failure domains and design recovery, telemetry, and preserved user work where possible.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

An error boundary does not catch every async/event-handler error automatically.

Presentational vs orchestration logic

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Separate UI rendering from workflow/data coordination when that separation clarifies responsibilities. It makes complex screens easier to test and redesign.

renders rows.

I separate orchestration from presentation when it reduces coupling, while avoiding rigid “container/ component” ceremony for simple cases.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

The boundary is a tool, not a mandatory folder pattern.

229 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE

Optimistic concurrency in UI

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Allow local interaction immediately, then reconcile with authoritative server state and version/conflict rules. It makes collaborative or latency-sensitive UIs feel fast without pretending conflicts cannot happen.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You pencil your name into the booking sheet, then the receptionist confirms whether someone else took the slot first.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Update UI -> send mutation with version ->
accept or rollback/conflict message.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Optimistic UI is strongest when paired with backend concurrency guarantees and a clear rollback/conflict strategy.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A pretty optimistic animation cannot fix duplicate writes or lost updates on the server.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 229 / 310

231 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Module

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A cohesive unit that exposes a public interface while hiding internal implementation details. Modules reduce the amount of code a developer must understand at once.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A microwave has buttons on the front; you do not need its wiring diagram to heat soup.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

payments/index.ts exports charge(); internal
gateway mapping stays private.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A good module has a focused responsibility, a small public surface, and internals that can change without breaking callers.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A folder is not automatically a module; the dependency boundary matters.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 231 / 310

232 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Encapsulation

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Hide internal state/implementation and expose only the operations consumers need. It prevents distant code from depending on fragile details.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You drive using steering wheel and pedals, not by reaching into the gearbox with your hand.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Cart exposes addItem(); callers do not mutate
cart.items internals directly.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how state and behavior are accessed.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Getters for every private field are not meaningful encapsulation if callers still control everything.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 232 / 310

233 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Abstraction

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A simplified model/interface that hides irrelevant detail for a particular task. It lets callers reason at the right level.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

“Send message” is useful; “open TCP socket, serialize bytes, retry packet 17…” is too low-level for most callers.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

storage.save(key,value) can hide whether storage
is IndexedDB or remote.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

An abstraction should hide volatility and expose the concepts consumers actually care about.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Bad abstractions hide important differences or force every implementation into the wrong shape.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 233 / 310

234 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Contract

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The behavior, inputs, outputs, errors, and guarantees that callers may rely on. Stable contracts let implementations evolve independently.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A restaurant promises “order before 10, receive food”; it does not promise which chef uses which pan.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

GET /users/:id returns User or 404 with
documented schema.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I design module/API contracts around observable behavior and keep implementation details out of the public surface.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Version or migrate breaking contract changes deliberately.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 234 / 310

235 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Dependency inversion

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

High-level business logic depends on abstractions/ capabilities rather than concrete infrastructure details. It reduces coupling to databases, vendors, and frameworks.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The lamp depends on “electricity from a socket,” not “this exact power station turbine #7.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

CheckoutService accepts PaymentGateway
interface; Stripe adapter implements it.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Dependency inversion keeps domain policy independent from replaceable infrastructure by depending on stable interfaces.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Do not invent interfaces for every class; use them where volatility or testing justifies the seam.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 235 / 310

236 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Ports and adapters

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Architecture where core logic exposes/consumes ports and external systems connect through adapters. It keeps domain behavior testable and independent from UI/database/vendor details.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The castle has standardized gates; horses, cars, and delivery robots can each use an adapter to enter.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Domain -> PaymentPort; StripePaymentAdapter ->
Stripe SDK.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Ports-and-adapters isolates core use cases from infrastructure and makes external integrations replaceable.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Useful when domain logic matters; excessive ceremony is wasteful for tiny CRUD apps.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 236 / 310

237 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Layered architecture

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Organize responsibilities into layers such as presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure. It creates dependency direction and reduces cross-cutting spaghetti.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Guests talk to the waiter, waiter to kitchen; guests do not sprint into the freezer.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

UI -> service/use case -> repository ->
database.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Layering is useful when each layer has a clear responsibility and dependencies mostly flow inward/ downward.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Avoid pass-through layers that add files but no semantic value.

238 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Pure core, imperative shell

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Keep business rules pure where possible and put I/O/ side effects at the edges. It makes critical logic deterministic and easy to test.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Do the math on paper first; only then call the bank, printer, and email robot.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

calculateQuote(input) is pure; handler fetches
DB data and sends result.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I isolate side effects at boundaries and keep core decision logic pure when practical.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

239 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Single Responsibility Principle

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A module should have one coherent reason to change. It prevents unrelated concerns from becoming entangled.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A Swiss Army knife is useful; a Swiss Army refrigerator-toaster-tax-accountant is not.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

InvoiceCalculator calculates totals; EmailSender
sends invoices.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

SRP is about reasons to change, not making every

function microscopic.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Over-splitting can create navigation overhead and weak abstractions.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 239 / 310

240 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Open/Closed Principle

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Prefer designs that allow new behavior through extension without repeatedly modifying fragile central logic. It can reduce regression risk in frequently extended systems.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Add a new train carriage instead of welding a new room into the locomotive engine each week.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Renderer registry maps type -> renderer instead
of a 500-line switch edited by every feature.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I use extension points where variation is proven and frequent; I do not pre-build plugin systems for hypothetical needs.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

YAGNI still applies.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 240 / 310

241 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Adapter pattern

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Wrap an incompatible or vendor-specific interface behind the interface your application wants. It contains third-party churn and translation logic.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A travel plug lets your German charger work in a UK socket without rebuilding the laptop.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

AnalyticsAdapter.track(event) wraps
VendorSDK.sendWeirdPayload(...).

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Adapters translate between boundaries and keep vendor-specific details from leaking through the codebase.

242 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Repository pattern

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

An abstraction representing access to domain data without exposing persistence mechanics to callers. It can isolate SQL/ORM details from use cases.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The librarian fetches books; you ask for ISBN 123, not “walk to shelf row 8 and run SQL.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

UserRepository.findById(id) -> User | null.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A repository can separate domain/application logic from persistence details, especially when queries and invariants deserve a stable interface.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Do not add repositories that are just thin copies of an ORM with no value.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 242 / 310

243 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Code smell

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A symptom suggesting design trouble, not proof of a bug. Smells guide investigation and refactoring.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Smoke does not always mean the house is burning, but you should probably look.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

12 boolean props, 900-line component, duplicated
conditional business rules.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Code smells are heuristics. I use them to ask why code is hard to change rather than applying automatic “clean code” rules.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Context matters: long code can be clearer than a premature abstraction.

244 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Refactoring

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Change internal structure while preserving externally observable behavior. It improves design safely when backed by tests and small steps.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Reorganize the kitchen cabinets without changing tonight's menu.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Extract pricing rule, rename types, split
module; tests keep behavior stable.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Refactoring improves structure without intentionally changing behavior. I prefer incremental, test-backed changes over big rewrites.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

A rewrite is not the same as a refactor.

245 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY

Feature flag

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A runtime or deployment control that enables behavior for selected users/environments. It decouples code deployment from feature release and supports safer rollout.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The roller coaster is built, but only staff with the green wristband may ride it today.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

if (flags.newCheckout) return <NewCheckout/>;

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Feature flags support gradual rollout and fast disablement, but need ownership and cleanup because stale flags become permanent branches.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Never rely on a frontend flag as an authorization boundary.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 245 / 310

246 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Normalization

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Structure relational data to reduce duplication and update anomalies, usually by separating distinct entities. It improves consistency and makes one fact have one authoritative home.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Do not write Grandma's phone number on 40 recipe cards; keep one contact record and reference it.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

orders.user_id -> users.id instead of copying
user email/address everywhere.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Normalization reduces duplicated facts and anomalies; I denormalize selectively when measured read patterns justify it.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Over-normalization can make read paths unnecessarily complex.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 246 / 310

247 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Denormalization

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Intentionally duplicate or precompute data to make reads simpler or faster. It trades write complexity/ storage for read performance.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Keep a snack in every room so you do not walk to the kitchen, but now every room needs restocking.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Store order_total on order instead of
recalculating from line items for every list
view.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Denormalization is a deliberate performance trade-off; I define how duplicated data stays consistent.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

If you cannot explain the synchronization rule, the duplicate may become corruption.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 247 / 310

248 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Database constraint

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A rule enforced by the database, such as NOT NULL, CHECK, UNIQUE, or FOREIGN KEY. It protects invariants even when multiple application paths write data.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

The nightclub door physically rejects anyone without a valid ticket; it does not trust every promoter to remember the rule.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

UNIQUE(email), CHECK(quantity > 0), FOREIGN KEY
user_id.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I enforce critical data invariants in the database as well as validating in the application.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Application validation gives nicer UX; database constraints give authoritative protection.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 248 / 310

249 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Unique constraint

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Guarantees that a value or combination of values cannot appear more than once. It closes race conditions that “check then insert” application logic cannot safely prevent alone.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two people race for username “wizard”; the database is the final referee.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

UNIQUE(tenant_id, slug)

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

A unique constraint is the authoritative way to enforce uniqueness under concurrency.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Catch and translate the constraint error into a useful domain response.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 249 / 310

250 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Composite index

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

An index built on multiple columns in a defined order. It can optimize queries filtering/sorting by those columns together.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

A phone book sorted by country then surname is great for “Germany + Müller” but not every possible lookup.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

INDEX(tenant_id, created_at DESC)

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Composite index column order should match important query predicates/sorts; I verify with query plans rather than guessing.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

More indexes increase write cost and storage.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 250 / 310

251 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Query plan

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The database's chosen strategy for executing a query. It reveals whether indexes, scans, joins, and estimates behave as expected.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

You ask for a route; the query plan is the GPS showing whether it takes the motorway or walks through a swamp.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I inspect query plans for slow queries to see actual scans, join strategies, row estimates, and index usage.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

“There is an index” does not mean the optimizer will use it.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 251 / 310

252 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Schema migration

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A controlled change to database structure or data as the application evolves. Production databases must change without losing data or breaking old/new app versions.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Renovate a hotel while guests are still sleeping inside.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

add nullable column -> deploy code -> backfill
-> enforce NOT NULL later.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

I design migrations for compatibility and rollback/ forward recovery, especially when deployments overlap versions.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Large locks and table rewrites can turn a harmless-looking migration into an outage.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 252 / 310

253 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Connection pool

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A managed set of reusable database connections shared by application requests. Opening a new DB connection per request is expensive and databases have finite connection capacity.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Keep 20 taxis ready instead of manufacturing a new car for every passenger.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

API process borrows a connection, runs query/
transaction, returns it to pool.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Connection pools amortize connection setup and cap concurrency, but pool size must respect total database capacity across app instances.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

100 app replicas x 50 connections can overwhelm a DB that supports 300.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 253 / 310

254 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Isolation level

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A transaction setting controlling which effects of concurrent transactions may be observed. It balances correctness guarantees against concurrency/ performance.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

How much can two accountants see of each other's half-finished spreadsheets?

R E A L   E X A M P L E

READ COMMITTED vs REPEATABLE READ vs
SERIALIZABLE.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Isolation levels define allowed concurrency phenomena. I choose based on the invariant rather than defaulting to the strongest level everywhere.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Database implementations differ in exact semantics; know your engine.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 254 / 310

255 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Deadlock

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Two transactions each hold resources the other needs, so neither can proceed. Concurrent locking can create circular waits.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Two people in a narrow hallway each refuse to step backward.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Tx A locks row 1 then wants 2; Tx B locks row 2
then wants 1.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Databases detect deadlocks and abort a participant; I keep transactions short, lock in consistent order, and retry safe failures.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Deadlock retries require idempotent transaction behavior.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 255 / 310

256 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Pessimistic locking

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Lock data before modifying it so competitors must wait. Useful when conflicts are likely and the cost of concurrent changes is high.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Put a “DO NOT TOUCH - I'M EDITING” sign on the only whiteboard.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Pessimistic locking serializes access to contested data, trading throughput for stronger coordination.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Long user-driven transactions holding DB locks are usually dangerous.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 256 / 310

257 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

MVCC

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Multi-Version Concurrency Control keeps multiple row versions so reads and writes can coexist with less blocking. It is a core reason modern relational databases can support concurrent transactions efficiently.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Readers get yesterday's newspaper copy while the editor prepares today's edition.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

Postgres snapshots let readers see a consistent
version while another transaction writes.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

MVCC uses row versions and transaction snapshots to provide isolation with reduced read/write blocking.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Old versions still require cleanup; long transactions can create bloat.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 257 / 310

258 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION

Read replica

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

A copy of a primary database used mainly to serve reads. It can scale read-heavy workloads and isolate analytics/reporting traffic.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

One chef writes the master recipe; many photocopies let 100 students read it.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

writes -> primary; product browse reads ->
replica.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Read replicas scale reads but introduce replication lag, so read-after-write consistency may need routing to primary.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Never assume a replica is instantly current.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 258 / 310

261 CACHING, PERFORMANCE & SCALABILITY

Cache-aside

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

The application checks cache first, loads from source on miss, then populates the cache. It is simple and common for read-heavy data.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Check the fridge; if milk is missing, go to the shop and put the new milk in the fridge.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

cache.get(key) -> miss -> db.query ->
cache.set(key,value,ttl).

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Cache-aside keeps the database authoritative while lazily populating cache on demand.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Plan for stale data, stampedes, and what happens when cache is unavailable.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 261 / 310

262 CACHING, PERFORMANCE & SCALABILITY

Write-through cache

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Writes update the cache and backing store as part of the write path. It keeps cached values fresh for subsequent reads.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Every time the restaurant changes the menu, both the kitchen board and website are updated before saying “done.”

R E A L   E X A M P L E

save user -> DB + cache before acknowledging.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Write-through improves cache freshness but increases write-path latency and couples availability to both systems unless carefully designed.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Failure ordering matters: which write succeeds first?

Explain it aloud before swiping. 262 / 310

263 CACHING, PERFORMANCE & SCALABILITY

Write-behind cache

I N   O N E   B R E AT H

Writes are accepted into cache/buffer and persisted to the backing store asynchronously. It can absorb bursts and reduce perceived write latency.

M A K E   I T   S T I C K

Drop letters into a mailbox now; the postal truck takes them to headquarters later.

R E A L   E X A M P L E

counter increments in cache; worker flushes
batches to durable store.

SAY   T H I S   I N   T H E   I N T E R V I E W

Write-behind can improve throughput but introduces durability and consistency risk if buffered writes are lost.

WATC H   /   L E V E L- U P

Use only when the data-loss window and recovery model are acceptable.

Explain it aloud before swiping. 263 / 310
